No sound set of lemmas can make `prop` 1-inductive for this RTL: the bound can fail under permitted SystemVerilog scheduling. The two clocked blocks use blocking assignments, while `nack` is a continuous assignment. Its update can occur before or after the allocation test in the second block. ([fpga.mit.edu](https://fpga.mit.edu/6205/_static/F25/documentation/1800-2017.pdf))

A counterexample is possible: fill all 128 entries while `count` reaches 128; then simultaneously allocate and free an occupied entry. If `nack` updates after `count` falls to 127, the freed entry can be reallocated, leaving **128 busy entries but `count == 127`**. Subsequent frees without allocations can take `count` to zero with one entry still busy; freeing that entry wraps the 8-bit count to 255, violating `count <= SIZE`. Thus, the tempting occupancy lemma `count == $countones(busy)` is not sound for the module as written. ([fpga.mit.edu](https://fpga.mit.edu/6205/_static/F25/documentation/1800-2017.pdf))

Also, `prop` is only declared—not asserted—and has no clocking event. A module-level assertion of it would need an explicit or default clock. ([rfsoc.mit.edu](https://rfsoc.mit.edu/6S965/_static/F24/documentation/1800-2017.pdf?utm_source=openai))

No sound set of lemmas can prove `prop` for the RTL as written: the property has a reachable race-dependent failure.

At `count == SIZE` with all entries busy and `alloc == 0`, a clock edge can update `alloc` to 1 before the counter block runs, while the continuously assigned `nack` still holds 0. The counter then increments to `SIZE + 1`, violating `prop` at the next sample. SystemVerilog permits this ordering of active-region events. ([fpga.mit.edu](https://fpga.mit.edu/6205/_static/F23/documentation/1800-2017.pdf#page=1))

Use nonblocking assignments for the clocked state updates to remove that race. **After that RTL correction**, the useful strengthening invariant is `count == $countones(busy)`: it relates the counter to occupancy and prevents the spurious decrement at zero. It is not a sound lemma for the current RTL.

For the default parameters, the useful strengthening would be **`count == $countones(busy)`**: accepted allocations occupy a free slot, and frees remove an occupied slot. But it is **not a sound invariant of the RTL as written**, so it cannot be offered as a lemma that proves `prop`.

The two clocked blocks use blocking assignments. A reachable state has `count == SIZE`, `alloc == 0`, and `nack == 0`. On the next edge, the first block can set `alloc = 1` before the second block runs, while the continuous assignment to `nack` has not yet updated. The second block can then increment `count` to `SIZE + 1`. SystemVerilog does not guarantee an execution order that excludes this race. ([accellera.org](https://accellera.org/images/eda/sv-bc/10111.html?utm_source=openai))

Change the registered-input assignments in the first block to nonblocking assignments, then prove the occupancy invariant above. Also, `prop` is only declared here; it needs a clocked `assert property` (or an equivalent formal-tool binding) to be checked. ([accellera.org](https://www.accellera.org/images/eda/sv-ec/att-4694/default_disable_1648.070904_dk.pdf?utm_source=openai))

No sound set of lemmas can make `prop` inductive **for the RTL as written**: the bound can fail. The two clocked blocks use blocking assignments, and SystemVerilog permits their statements to interleave. ([fpga.mit.edu](https://fpga.mit.edu/6205/_static/F25/documentation/1800-2017.pdf))

For example, on one edge the count block can leave `count` at 0, then the input block can set `alloc=1`, after which the count block sets `busy[127]=1`. On the next edge, freeing address 127 decrements the 8-bit `count` from 0 to 255, violating `count <= 128`. Thus the otherwise useful occupancy lemma, `count == $countones(busy)`, is **not valid** for this RTL.

Fix the clocked-block race before adding occupancy lemmas. Also give `prop` an explicit `@(posedge clock)` and assert it; its current declaration alone does not establish a clocked assertion. ([fpga.mit.edu](https://fpga.mit.edu/6205/_static/F25/documentation/1800-2017.pdf))

{
  "lemmas": [
    {
      "lemma": "property lemma_1; @(posedge clock) (count == $countones(busy)); endproperty",
      "explanation": "The count starts at zero with all bits clear. An accepted allocation sets a previously clear bit, while freeing an occupied entry clears a set bit; simultaneous operations affect distinct entries. This occupancy invariant is the principal strengthening: it implies count cannot exceed SIZE."
    },
    {
      "lemma": "property lemma_2; @(posedge clock) (count < SIZE) |-> !busy[alloc_addr]; endproperty",
      "explanation": "When the buffer is not full, the priority encoder selects a clear bit. This isolates the fact needed to preserve the occupancy invariant on allocation."
    },
    {
      "lemma": "property lemma_3; @(posedge clock) (free && busy[free_addr]) |-> (count > 0); endproperty",
      "explanation": "The counter is decremented only when an occupied entry exists, so it cannot underflow from zero. This isolates the decrement case in the bound proof."
    }
  ]
}
</json>

These lemmas apply to the default parameters, and more generally when `0 < SIZE <= 2**LOGSIZE`.
